# Input

```{r}
#Libraries
library(pacman)
p_load(lavaan, rio, tidyverse, psych, here, stargazer, summarytools, visdat,
       EGAnet, qgraph, ggplot2, haven, janitor, readxl, labelled, reshape2,
       openxlsx, mgm, bootnet, conflicted, magick, cocron, lme4, broom.mixed, 
       patchwork, huge, grid)

#Options
rm(list = ls())
options(scipen = 999)
#conflicts
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

# Data
# master_datasets.rds is built by script 1 and is included in this repository, so this script
# runs as-is. The raw Study 2 and Study 3 files that script 1 starts from are not redistributed
# here: see the note at the top of 1_Data_Managment.Rmd, or "Data sources" in the README,
# for how to download them from the Harvard Dataverse.
master_datasets <- readRDS(here("Input", "Secondary", "master_datasets.rds"))
```

# Processing

## Preparation

```{r}
# Initialize an empty list for H2
H2_matrices <- list()

# Loop through the master list to extract and split data 
for (study_name in names(master_datasets)) {
  
  df <- master_datasets[[study_name]]
  
  # For H2 we keep only country, the CB sum-score, and individual cm_ items
  df_clean <- df %>%
    select(country, CB, starts_with("cm_")) %>%
    na.omit()
  
  # Split by country
  split_df <- split(df_clean[, setdiff(names(df_clean), "country")], df_clean$country)
  
  # Convert to matrices, apply nonparanormal transformation, and assign names
  for (country_name in names(split_df)) {
    list_name <- paste0(study_name, "_", country_name)
    
    # 1. Convert to raw matrix
    raw_matrix <- as.matrix(split_df[[country_name]])
    
    # 2. Apply the nonparanormal transformation directly
    # This relaxes Gaussian assumptions for the skewed conspiracy items
    H2_matrices[[list_name]] <- huge.npn(raw_matrix, verbose = FALSE)
  }
}
```

## Network estimation and plotting

```{r}
# ONE ESTIMATOR FOR THE WHOLE PAPER.
# Every network in this paper, drawn or analysed, is estimated with mgm() under EBIC
# (lambdaGam = 0.25) and the AND rule. These are exactly the settings bootnet(default = "mgm")
# applies internally, so the pictures below show the same networks the Strength estimates,
# the bootstrap intervals and the difference tests are computed on. Script 6 re-runs the
# H1 and H2 analyses under cross-validation, with the AND and then the OR rule. Ranks are
# identical in all 34 networks and verdicts in 32 of 34; the German and British H1 networks
# move from falsified to inconclusive, which Section 5.5 reports.
# The seed is kept for the layout algorithm rather than for the fit: EBIC selection is
# deterministic, but qgraph's spring placement is not.
set.seed(123)

# Maintain color consistency: Purple for CM items, Green for CB Index
Totalgroup_cols_H2 <- c("#966FD6", "#006B3C") 

for (name in names(H2_matrices)) {
  
  data_matrix <- H2_matrices[[name]]
  n_vars <- ncol(data_matrix)
  node_names <- colnames(data_matrix)
  
  # Generate type and level (all Gaussian after huge.npn)
  type_vec <- rep("g", n_vars)
  level_vec <- rep(1, n_vars)
  
  # Estimation using MGM
  mgm_result <- mgm(
    data_matrix, type = type_vec, level = level_vec,
    lambdaSel = "EBIC", lambdaGam = 0.25, ruleReg = "AND", verbose = FALSE, pbar = FALSE
  )
  
  # Predictability (R2 pie charts)
  pred_result <- predict(object = mgm_result, data = data_matrix, errorCon = 'R2')
  
  # Assign groups for H2: CM items vs. the single CB sum-score
  groups_H2 <- list(
    "CM items" = which(grepl("^cm_", node_names)),
    "CB Index" = which(node_names == "CB")
  )
  
  # Output path for high-res PNG
  output_path <- here("Output", "H2", "Country_networks", paste0(name, ".png"))

  # Open PNG device (High Resolution)
  png(output_path, width = 4.15, height = 5.85, units = "in", res = 600)

  # Generate the qgraph plot 
  qgraph(
    mgm_result$pairwise$wadj, 
    layout = "spring", 
    labels = node_names,
    groups = groups_H2,   
    color = Totalgroup_cols_H2, 
    legend = FALSE,
    title = name, 
    edge.color = mgm_result$pairwise$edgecolor_cb, # colourblind-safe, as in scripts 2 and 3
    vTrans = 180, 
    borders = TRUE, 
    vsize = 10, 
    esize = 7, 
    label.cex = 0.50,
    label.scale = FALSE, 
    pie = pred_result$errors[,2], 
    pieColor = rep('#FFFF00', n_vars)
  )

  dev.off()
}
```

## Final visualization for the paper

```{r}
# manage data again
H1_matrices <- list()
H2_matrices <- list()

for (study_name in names(master_datasets)) {
  df <- master_datasets[[study_name]]
  
  # Re-build H1 matrices 
  df_h1 <- df %>% select(country, CM, starts_with("cb_")) %>% na.omit()
  split_h1 <- split(df_h1[, setdiff(names(df_h1), "country")], df_h1$country)
  for (cn in names(split_h1)) {
    H1_matrices[[paste0(study_name, "_", cn)]] <- huge.npn(as.matrix(split_h1[[cn]]), verbose = FALSE)
  }
  
  # Re-build H2 matrices 
  df_h2 <- df %>% select(country, CB, starts_with("cm_")) %>% na.omit()
  split_h2 <- split(df_h2[, setdiff(names(df_h2), "country")], df_h2$country)
  for (cn in names(split_h2)) {
    H2_matrices[[paste0(study_name, "_", cn)]] <- huge.npn(as.matrix(split_h2[[cn]]), verbose = FALSE)
  }
}

# load h1 results
boot_results_H1 <- readRDS(here("Input", "Secondary", "boot_H1_master.rds"))


# process boots again
process_boots <- function(boot_list, matrix_list, hypo_label) {
  lapply(names(boot_list), function(name) {
    boot_table <- boot_list[[name]][["bootTable"]]
    values <- boot_table[["value"]]
    node_names <- colnames(matrix_list[[name]])
    n_nodes <- length(node_names)
    # same safety check on the bootTable ordering
    stopifnot(all(as.character(boot_table[["node1"]]) ==
                    rep(node_names, length.out = nrow(boot_table))))
    df <- as.data.frame(matrix(values, ncol = n_nodes, byrow = TRUE))
    colnames(df) <- node_names
    df$Dataset <- name
    df$Hypothesis <- hypo_label
    melt(df, id.vars = c("Dataset", "Hypothesis"), variable.name = "Node", value.name = "Centrality")
  }) %>% bind_rows()
}

long_h1 <- process_boots(boot_results_H1, H1_matrices, "H1")
long_h2 <- process_boots(boot_results_H2, H2_matrices, "H2")
all_long_data <- bind_rows(long_h1, long_h2)

# Labeling 
all_long_data <- all_long_data %>%
  mutate(
    CountryRaw = str_remove_all(Dataset, "Study1_SUSPECTS_|Study2_ACTS_|Study3_CMQ_"),
    CountryName = case_when(
      CountryRaw == "DEU" ~ "Germany",
      CountryRaw == "ESP" ~ "Spain",
      CountryRaw == "FRA" ~ "France",
      CountryRaw == "GBR" ~ "United Kingdom",
      CountryRaw == "ITA" ~ "Italy",
      CountryRaw == "POL" ~ "Poland",
      CountryRaw == "SWE" ~ "Sweden",
      CountryRaw %in% c("USA", "USA_ACTS") ~ "United States",
      TRUE ~ CountryRaw
    ),
    Scale = case_when(
      grepl("Study1", Dataset) ~ "GCB5",
      grepl("Study2", Dataset) ~ "ACTS",
      grepl("Study3_CMQ", Dataset) ~ "CMQ"
    )
  )

all_ci_data <- all_long_data %>%
  group_by(CountryName, Scale, Node, Hypothesis) %>%
  summarise(lower = quantile(Centrality, probs = 0.025),
            upper = quantile(Centrality, probs = 0.975), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#Define a global theme
theme_masterpiece <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11, base_family = "serif") +
    theme(
      # Text elements
      text = element_text(family = "serif", color = "#1A1A1A"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, family = "serif", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
      plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22, family = "serif"),
      
      # Facet Strip
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#EFEFEF", color = "#333333", size = 0.6),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, family = "serif", color = "#1A1A1A"),
      
      # Grid Logic
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#D1D1D1", size = 0.4, linetype = "dotted"),
      
      # Background
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#333333", size = 0.7),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#F9F9F7", color = NA), 
      
      # Axis Styling
      axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, margin = margin(r = 12)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8.5, color = "black", face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(color = "#333333", size = 0.5),
      
      # Legend 
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
}

# High-Contrast "Scientific" Colors
node_colors <- c("Index" = "#702963", "Item" = "#008080")
```

```{r}
# Saving the article figures.
#
# Every article figure is written twice, into Output/Figures/:
#   - a PNG at 600 dpi, named after the figure caption, for reading in this repository;
#   - a vector PDF named Figure_1.pdf ... Figure_4.pdf, for the publisher.
#
# The canvas is 180 x 220 mm. Wiley asks for artwork created between 80 and 180 mm wide,
# so 180 mm is the full-width option and it means production does not have to rescale
# anything: the point sizes in theme_masterpiece() are what gets printed. Their naming
# rule for production files is the word "figure" plus the number and nothing else, which
# is why the PDFs are named that way and only the PNGs carry the descriptive titles.

fig_dir <- here("Output", "Figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

FIG_W_MM <- 180
FIG_H_MM <- 220
mm_to_in <- function(x) x / 25.4

# Descriptive names for the PNGs, mirroring the captions in the article.
# No colons: they are illegal in Windows file names and awkward everywhere else.
fig_titles <- c(
  "1" = "Figure 1 - conspiracy belief systems in the U.S",
  "2" = "Figure 2 - Study 1 results",
  "3" = "Figure 3 - Study 2 results",
  "4" = "Figure 4 - Study 3 results"
)

save_article_figure <- function(plot_obj, number,
                                width_mm = FIG_W_MM, height_mm = FIG_H_MM) {

  w <- mm_to_in(width_mm)
  h <- mm_to_in(height_mm)

  # Vector version for production
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0("Figure_", number, ".pdf")),
         plot = plot_obj, device = cairo_pdf,
         width = w, height = h, units = "in")

  # Raster version for the repository
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(fig_titles[[as.character(number)]], ".png")),
         plot = plot_obj, device = "png", type = "cairo",
         width = w, height = h, units = "in", dpi = 600)

  invisible(NULL)
}
```

p1_s1 <- all_long_data %>%

  geom_errorbar(data = filter(all_ci_data, Scale == "GCB5", Hypothesis == "H1"),

  theme_masterpiece() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)))

# Panel b
p2_s1 <- all_long_data %>% 
  filter(Scale == "GCB5", Hypothesis == "H2") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Node, y = Centrality)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = ifelse(Node == "CB", "Index", "Item")), 
               width = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", size = 0.7, coef = 0) +
  geom_errorbar(data = filter(all_ci_data, Scale == "GCB5", Hypothesis == "H2"),
                aes(x = Node, ymin = lower, ymax = upper), 
                width = 0.15, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ CountryName, ncol = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = node_colors) +
  labs(y = "Strength Centrality", tag = "B", title = "H2") +
  theme_masterpiece() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)))

# together
combined_s1 <- (p1_s1 / p2_s1) + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1)) & 
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    # 9 rotated labels inside a 45 mm facet collide at the theme's 8.5 pt on
    # Wiley's 180 mm canvas, which is narrower than the one these panels were
    # first drawn on. 6 pt clears them.
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6)
  )

# Figure 2 in the article
save_article_figure(combined_s1, number = 2)

### Analytical strategy plot

```{r}
# a figure explaining the logic behind our networks

# manage data as before
df_usa <- master_datasets[["Study1_SUSPECTS"]] %>% 
  filter(country == "USA") %>% 
  select(CM, CB, starts_with("cb_"), starts_with("cm_")) %>% 
  na.omit()

m0 <- huge.npn(as.matrix(df_usa %>% select(starts_with("cb_"), starts_with("cm_"))), verbose = FALSE)
m1 <- huge.npn(as.matrix(df_usa %>% select(CM, starts_with("cb_"))), verbose = FALSE)
m2 <- huge.npn(as.matrix(df_usa %>% select(CB, starts_with("cm_"))), verbose = FALSE)

# colors
cols_index <- "#702963"
cols_item  <- "#008080"

# Fit the three networks once.
# Same estimator as everywhere else in the paper: EBIC with lambdaGam = 0.25 and the AND
# rule, i.e. the settings bootnet(default = "mgm") uses for the Strength estimates in
# Figures 2 to 4. EBIC selection is deterministic, so these three fits do not depend on the
# seed; it is set for the layout algorithm below.
set.seed(123)

fit0 <- mgm(m0, type = rep("g", ncol(m0)), level = rep(1, ncol(m0)),
            lambdaSel = "EBIC", lambdaGam = 0.25, ruleReg = "AND", verbose = FALSE, pbar = FALSE)
fit1 <- mgm(m1, type = rep("g", ncol(m1)), level = rep(1, ncol(m1)),
            lambdaSel = "EBIC", lambdaGam = 0.25, ruleReg = "AND", verbose = FALSE, pbar = FALSE)
fit2 <- mgm(m2, type = rep("g", ncol(m2)), level = rep(1, ncol(m2)),
            lambdaSel = "EBIC", lambdaGam = 0.25, ruleReg = "AND", verbose = FALSE, pbar = FALSE)

# Freeze the spring layouts.
#
# Two problems forced this. First, qgraph rescales a "spring" layout to the plotting region,
# so the same network laid out on two devices with different aspect ratios comes out arranged
# differently, and this figure is written to both a PNG and a PDF. Second, the
# Fruchterman-Reingold placement is not reproducible: it varies from session to session, and
# set.seed() does not control it, because the randomness is not in R's RNG. I checked this
# directly - three fresh sessions with set.seed(123) returned layouts summing to 14.233,
# 14.208 and 14.187.
#
# So I compute the coordinates once and keep them. The two output files then show the same
# picture, and anyone re-running this script gets the figure that is in the paper rather than
# a new arrangement of it. Delete the .rds if you want to draw a fresh layout.
#
# The stored coordinates were regenerated for the EBIC/AND networks. A layout computed on the
# older CV/OR fits would place nodes for a network that is no longer the one being drawn, so
# the file was deleted and rebuilt when the estimator changed.

layout_file <- here("Input", "Secondary", "figure1_layouts.rds")

if (file.exists(layout_file)) {
  figure1_layouts <- readRDS(layout_file)
} else {
  fixed_layout <- function(fit) {
    qgraph(fit$pairwise$wadj, layout = "spring", minimum = 0.03, DoNotPlot = TRUE)$layout
  }
  figure1_layouts <- list(H0 = fixed_layout(fit0),
                          H1 = fixed_layout(fit1),
                          H2 = fixed_layout(fit2))
  saveRDS(figure1_layouts, layout_file)
}

lay0 <- figure1_layouts$H0
lay1 <- figure1_layouts$H1
lay2 <- figure1_layouts$H2

# The layouts must match the networks they are drawn on
stopifnot(nrow(lay0) == ncol(m0), nrow(lay1) == ncol(m1), nrow(lay2) == ncol(m2))

# function to plot networks
# Node size is set per panel. The three panels hold 13, 9 and 6 nodes in strips of the same
# width, so a single vsize either crowds H0 or leaves H2 looking sparse.
plot_usa_net_titled <- function(fit, layout_matrix, labs, groups, title_text, vsize) {

  qgraph(fit$pairwise$wadj,
         layout = layout_matrix,
         labels = labs,
         groups = groups,
         color = c(cols_index, cols_item),
         edge.color = fit$pairwise$edgecolor_cb,
         minimum = 0.03,
         title = title_text,
         title.cex = 2.5,
         vsize = vsize,
         label.cex = 1.1,
         edge.width = 1,
         trans = 0.8,
         borders = TRUE,
         border.width = 1.5,
         legend = FALSE,
         mar = c(4, 4, 7, 4))
}

# Assembly.
# This one is base graphics rather than ggplot, so it cannot go through
# save_article_figure(). I draw it twice instead, once per device, from the same code.

draw_figure_1 <- function() {
  # H0 gets the tallest strip because it carries all 13 items at once
  layout(matrix(1:3, ncol = 1), heights = c(1.35, 1, 0.95))
  par(family = "serif", font.main = 2)

  # H0
  plot_usa_net_titled(fit0, lay0, colnames(m0),
                      list("CB" = which(startsWith(colnames(m0), "cb_")),
                           "CM" = which(startsWith(colnames(m0), "cm_"))),
                      "H0", vsize = 11)
  # H1
  plot_usa_net_titled(fit1, lay1, colnames(m1),
                      list("Index" = 1, "Items" = 2:ncol(m1)),
                      "H1", vsize = 14)
  # H2
  plot_usa_net_titled(fit2, lay2, colnames(m2),
                      list("Index" = 1, "Items" = 2:ncol(m2)),
                      "H2", vsize = 15)
}

# Vector version for production
# Figure 1 is taller than the others: three stacked networks need the room.
FIG1_H_MM <- 240

cairo_pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "Figure_1.pdf"),
          width = mm_to_in(FIG_W_MM), height = mm_to_in(FIG1_H_MM),
          bg = "#F9F9F7")
draw_figure_1()
dev.off()

# Raster version for the repository
png(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(fig_titles[["1"]], ".png")),
    width = mm_to_in(FIG_W_MM), height = mm_to_in(FIG1_H_MM), units = "in", res = 600,
    type = "cairo", bg = "#F9F9F7")
draw_figure_1()
dev.off()

```
